events.title: Philosophy of Mind: AI and Consciousness
events.description: UQ's Professor of Philosophy presents her latest research on the hard problem of consciousness and what AI systems can and cannot tell us about subjective experience. Aimed at a general audience with no background in philosophy required. Followed by a 30-minute open Q&A.
events.why: One of UQ's leading philosophers speaking publicly on a genuinely hard topic — the Q&A format means you can actually engage with her.

events.title: Open Mic Night — Archive Bar
events.description: Weekly open mic night in a cosy West End bar. Anyone can sign up on the night for a 5-minute slot — originals and covers both welcome. Regular crowd of musicians, writers, and neighbourhood locals who actually listen.
events.why: One of Brisbane's most genuinely welcoming open mics — the host keeps the vibe warm and the audience actually pays attention.

events.title: Introduction to Wheel Throwing — Pottery Workshop
events.description: A 3-hour beginner workshop learning to centre and throw clay on a kick wheel. All materials and tools provided. The studio keeps class sizes small — maximum 8 participants — so you get real attention from the instructor.
events.why: BY.ARTISANS keeps class sizes tiny and the instructors are working artists — you actually learn rather than just making a mess.

events.title: CreativeMornings Brisbane — Trust
events.description: Monthly free breakfast lecture series for the creative community. This month's speaker is a Brisbane-based documentary filmmaker speaking on trust — in collaborators, in subjects, in audiences. Doors open at 7:30 AM for coffee and conversation.
events.why: Reliably one of the best free events in Brisbane — the pre-talk breakfast means you actually talk to people rather than just sitting in rows.

events.title: QAGOMA: Surrealism Now — Opening Night
events.location: Gallery of Modern Art (GOMA), South Bank
events.description: Opening night for QAGOMA's major winter exhibition examining surrealism in contemporary practice. Works from 40 Australian and international artists across painting, sculpture, and video installation. Free entry; drinks available from the gallery bar.
events.why: GOMA's opening nights draw Brisbane's art crowd and the works in this show are genuinely strange and ambitious — not the usual safe gallery fare.

events.title: Avid Reader: Author Talk — Richard Fidler
events.description: Richard Fidler, ABC broadcaster and author, discusses his new book on Byzantine Constantinople. Fidler's Conversations podcast has a devoted following; his talks are warm, detailed, and genuinely illuminating. Books available to purchase and sign on the night.
events.why: Fidler is one of Australia's best oral storytellers — hearing him talk about his research in a small bookshop is a very different experience to the podcast.

events.title: Queensland Symphony Orchestra — Mahler 5
events.description: The QSO performs Mahler's Fifth Symphony under guest conductor Elena Schwartz. One of Mahler's most emotionally powerful works, running approximately 75 minutes. Pre-concert talk at 6:30 PM included with ticket.
events.why: Mahler 5 is one of the great war-horses of the orchestral repertoire and this conductor has a reputation for letting it breathe.

events.title: UQ Science Public Lecture: The Microbiome
events.location: UQ Oral Health Centre Auditorium, Herston
events.description: Associate Professor of Microbiology explores what the gut microbiome actually is, how it affects mood and cognition, and what the current research does and doesn't support. One of UQ's popular public science series, aimed at curious non-specialists.
events.why: UQ's science public lectures are well-organised and this topic cuts through a lot of pseudoscience — worth going for the Q&A alone.

events.title: Experimental Film Screening — Institute of Modern Art
events.description: IMA screens three short films by Brisbane-based video artists working with archival footage and generative AI. Followed by a panel discussion with the artists and IMA curator. Runtime approximately 90 minutes including discussion.
events.why: IMA consistently programmes challenging work — the panel format means you get the artists' actual thinking rather than just a wall label.

events.title: Language Exchange — French & English
events.description: Informal weekly language exchange at a friendly city café. Half the session in French, half in English. Mix of expats, travellers, and locals learning for fun. No formal structure — just conversation over coffee.
events.why: Genuinely social rather than classroom-style — the café setting means it feels like you're just having a drink with interesting people.

events.title: Drag Bingo — Come to Daddy
events.description: Monthly drag-hosted bingo night at West End's queer bar. Host Destiny Disaster runs a chaotic and very funny evening with prizes, lip sync performances between rounds, and genuinely terrible bingo puns. First drink included with entry.
events.why: Destiny Disaster is one of Brisbane's funniest drag performers and the crowd is exactly the kind of warm, weird mix that makes a Saturday night memorable.

events.title: Beginners Watercolour Workshop
events.description: A 2.5-hour afternoon workshop for complete beginners in watercolour painting. Working artist guides participants through basic wash techniques, colour mixing, and a simple landscape. All materials included. Maximum 12 participants.
events.why: Lightspace runs these well — the instructor is patient and the venue is an actual art space, not a community hall.

events.title: Black Bear Lodge: Thursday Jazz Night
events.description: Weekly jazz night featuring a rotating cast of Brisbane jazz musicians. Intimate bar setting with no cover charge. The Thursday residency has been running for three years and tends to attract serious jazz heads as well as curious walk-ins.
events.why: The Thursday residency at Black Bear has become a genuine institution — the musicians are good and the room is the right size for jazz.

events.title: Griffith University Public Lecture: Climate Migration
events.description: Griffith's Centre for Governance and Public Policy hosts a lecture on climate-induced migration patterns in the Pacific and what international legal frameworks do and don't cover. Presenter has spent five years working with Pacific island communities. Q&A follows.
events.why: Griffith has strong Pacific research connections and this presenter has field experience rather than just academic theory.

events.title: South Bank Parklands: Sunday Circus
events.description: Free outdoor performance featuring local circus and acrobatics groups in South Bank's Riverside Green. Approximately 45 minutes of juggling, aerial silks, and acrobatics. Family-friendly, no bookings required.
events.why: A genuinely enjoyable free hour if you're already at South Bank — the performers are students from a local circus school and consistently impressive.
